chunks: "I like to group applications by how the light is used. Passive: measure the light that is already there.
Ambient light sensors set screen and keyboard brightness, so phones and laptops save power and look right, and they drive automatic headlights and street lights.
A camera light meter sets exposure. Colour sensors adjust a display's white point to the room. Active reflective: add my own LED and look at the light that comes back.
A proximity sensor in a phone pulses an infrared LED and measures how much reflects from your face, to turn off the screen.
A smoke detector looks for an LED beam scattered by smoke.
Heart-rate and pulse-oximetry sensors shine red and infrared LEDs through the skin and measure how the absorption changes with each heartbeat; the ratio of the two wavelengths gives blood oxygen.
Transmissive: optical encoders, slot sensors and light curtains detect a beam being interrupted, so I get position, speed or presence.
Ranging and imaging: LiDAR and time-of-flight sensors measure the delay of a pulse, and cameras are arrays of photodiodes.
Communications: IR remotes, fibre receivers and optocouplers detect modulated light.
The recurring design problem is ambient light and dynamic range: sunlight can be a million times brighter than my signal, so I modulate the source, AC-couple, and subtract the LED-off reading."
